name: tts-cpp
description: Text-to-speech in pure C++/ggml: Resemble Chatterbox (Turbo + Multilingual), Supertonic, Fun-CosyVoice3, Parler-TTS (CPU + Metal / Vulkan / OpenCL GPU), and LavaSR speech enhancement. Sourced from tetherto/qvac-ext-lib-whisper.cpp (engines/tts). This pin (master HEAD 1823ab31, PR #118) runs CosyVoice3 on the GPU. It had landed CPU-only: cosyvoice_load_gguf() hardcoded a CPU backend, all six graphs computed through it directly, and n_gpu_layers / backends_dir were declared but never read. Three things blocked the GPU path and are fixed here. mish() built log(exp(x)+1) around a `one` tensor created under no_alloc=false -- host malloc, no buffer, so the first ggml_cl_add would dereference null -- and is replaced by ggml_softplus, which is 100.0000% bit-identical over 960001 samples spanning x in [-120,120], drops GGML_OP_LOG (which ggml-opencl does not implement), and stops generating the +inf intermediate the old form produced for every x > 88. build_lm_input() and cosyvoice_llm_generate() read two weights through ggml_get_data(), but ggml-opencl's buffer_get_base() returns a small sentinel, so that is a segfault rather than a slow read; those two tables are never graph operands, so they now stay host-resident, which also keeps 545 MB of embed_tokens off the device. And conv1d_grouped now emits one 2-D convolution per (group, batch) so the Adreno im2col fusion can claim it. Measured on an Adreno 740: 2.04-2.15x faster than the same device's CPU, thermally gated with equal work asserted on every leg. This release also completes PR #117's dl-safety fix: removing the `one` tensor drops the last ggml_new_f32 call, which #117 fixed in cosyvoice_pipeline.cpp but left in the standalone cosyvoice_flow.cpp, where it fails to link under GGML_BACKEND_DL=ON. The ggml-speech floor moves to 2026-08-03: the vocoder's speed depends on that pin's unaligned-M im2col fusion (PR #50), without which CausalHiFT is correct but falls back to the slow local-memory GEMM. Carries the dl-safe backend init (PR #117), the bounded Parler DAC decode (PR #114), the full Parler pipeline on Vulkan (PR #110), the Metal GPU pin (PR #103), and the original CosyVoice3 pin (PR #99). CPU output is byte-identical.
